proposal.method_text:
H v3: triage-first, world-branched, rehearsal-gated design ledger. Instructions to the consuming run. This H supplies reads, inequalities and change directions only; it supplies no design-field values, and every number in a run is bound to a named field of that run's own sources.

STEP 0 - Entry ledger (write before any other step, and keep verbatim).
Record: base artifact id and hash (H0 1784856e) and the immutable proposal prefix hash (01bf9c13); the action set actually offered to this consumer; and, per referenced episode, whether a design check existed - p2 was offered a check and got ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE, recorded as UNKNOWN, never pass or fail; p3's check ran and returned physical_qualification = UNKNOWN, which stays UNKNOWN. Record for every acquisition: source_id, source_sha256, and the returned block (bytes, native_calls, new_scientific_executions, wall_seconds) as actual cost. In the episode that produced this draft, acquisitions of component_record, excitation_record and saved_activity each returned UNKNOWN_PUBLIC_SOURCE: record that as UNKNOWN exposure of those families, spend nothing further on it, and never substitute another episode's values for a family this run does not expose. A source family that is missing or unavailable is UNKNOWN data, not a pass, not a fail and not a zero. No step below may depend on a check being offered; if the consumer's action set contains no check, every design it drafts stays UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN and this ledger is its only evidence.

STEP 1 - Triage-first reading (mandatory first diagnostic step, taken before any diagnosis or change).
Classify each retained observation against the service fields alone:
  ACHIEVED iff a packet exists whose application_bytes equals the required bytes, carrying a single event id, with packet time at or before the receive deadline (fields: saved_activity packets[*].application_bytes, .event_id, .time_s against the task's required bytes, unique-frame count and deadline).
  POST-TERMINAL: any activity event whose time is strictly after the last action = tx-complete is expected decay once the source segments end; record it as benign, log it, and never treat it as grounds for a knob change.
  RETAINED FAILURE: only an absent ACHIEVED delivery, or one that violates a service field. Sub-class it as (a) deadline miss, (b) threshold/boot-domain failure (energy never reached the ready threshold), (c) capture lost to a brownout that strictly precedes a tx-complete, (d) frame-shape violation (bytes, frame count, duplicate event id).
Do not read a post-terminal brownout as the failure even when it is the last activity record, and do not read a pre-terminal brownout as benign even when the final state looks discharged.

STEP 2 - World branching (read per run; one world's numbers are never transplanted into the other).
Read from the component record: event_latch class; capacitance; ready, off and maximum rated capacitor voltages; initial capacitor voltage; boot energy; boot delay; series resistance; output voltage; transmit current and duration; off-state and idle/awake power; harvest efficiency.
Read from the excitation record: timestep; every source segment (start, end, power, compliance); every shunt entry (time, energy); any contact duration; the deadline.
Branch (i) latch: 'volatile' means the capture survives only while the rail stays above the off threshold continuously from first capture through tx-complete, so a brownout in that interval destroys the event and the design must satisfy a retention inequality, not merely an energy-one. 'passive-mechanical' means capture survives unpowered gaps, so timing gates are energy gates and the retention inequality is recorded as non-binding. Branch (ii) source shape: classify as SINGLE_SEGMENT when there is one contiguous powered interval, or SEGMENTED_WITH_GAP when two or more segments are separated by a zero-power interval, with any shunt treated as an instantaneous energy removal at its recorded time; note that the recorded dark gap is the interval in which the only available energy is storage. Branch (iii) never assume thresholds: take ready/off/max voltages, efficiency and leakage from the record, and state explicitly which named field each came from.

STEP 3 - Symbolic ledger (a prediction computed from fields, not a result).
Define, for the run's own fields: step_charge(p) = (p * harvest_efficiency - off_power_w) * dt inside a segment of power p; step_idle = -off_power_w * dt outside all segments; an awake tick drains idle_power_w * dt instead. E_ready = 0.5 * C * ready_v^2; E_off = 0.5 * C * off_v^2; E_max = 0.5 * C * cap_voltage_max_v^2. Threshold-first boot: n_boot = ceil((E_ready - E_init) / step_charge(p_first_segment)) counting ticks from cap_initial_voltage_v, so t_boot = n_boot * dt and stored energy immediately after boot = n_boot * step_charge - boot_j - (boot energy is deducted after the threshold is met, never folded into the threshold, and boot_delay_s is a separate awake-to-ready offset, so t_ready = t_boot + boot_delay_s). Transmit floor comes from the model's loaded-voltage guard, not from the off threshold: E_txfloor = 0.5 * C * (output_v + esr_ohm * tx_current_a)^2, which sits slightly above E_off while transmitting. Transmit budget per tick: step_tx = p * harvest_efficiency * dt - idle_power_w * dt - output_v * tx_current_a * dt inside a segment, and -idle_power_w * dt - output_v * tx_current_a * dt outside; n_tx = ceil(tx_duration_s / dt); t_done = max(t_ready, tx_not_before_s) + n_tx * dt; E_tx = output_v * tx_current_a * tx_duration_s.
Log four inequalities with their numeric margins computed from this run's fields:
  (i) t_done <= deadline.
  (ii) stored energy at t_ready + sum of step_tx over the transmit window - E_txfloor >= 0, i.e. the transmission completes without a mid-frame reset.
  (iii) predicted peak stored energy over [t_boot, t_done] <= E_max, so no spill.
  (iv) retention: if event_latch is volatile, no tick between first capture and t_done has stored energy below E_off; if passive-mechanical, record (iv) as non-binding rather than as satisfied.
Post-terminal decay is computed for triage only and never for a knob change: t_terminal = (last segment end) >= t_done, then brownout when storage falls to E_off under awake drain, i.e. (stored near segment end - E_off) / drain_power; report both drain candidates (idle/awake power if the model keeps the device awake after done, off power otherwise) and keep the candidate that matches the record.

STEP 4 - Change-or-retain decision rules.
4.1 If step 1 is ACHIEVED and the currently recorded design satisfies (i)-(iv) with positive margins, RETAIN it, spend no execution, and record post-terminal events as benign.
4.2 If step 1 is a RETAINED FAILURE, name its sub-class, then change exactly one legal design field in the direction the sign of the violated inequality demands (raise or lower stored energy, lengthen or shorten the powered window needed before transmit, relax the transmit floor, extend retention), re-evaluate (i)-(iv) for every candidate inside the legal ranges read from inspect, and only then spend a single execution. Never change two fields in one execution; never spend an execution on a post-terminal event; respect the recorded candidate/distinct-design budget and log the actual cost of each execution.
4.3 Prefer the setting that maximizes the minimum normalized margin across (i)-(iv); report ties and both band edges together with the inequality that fails at each edge.

STEP 5 - UNKNOWN, rehearsal and retention rules.
5.1 Rehearse before proposing: instantiate this H on a frozen episode that already has recorded observations, recompute t_boot, t_ready, t_done, the four margins and the decay time from that episode's own fields, and compare tick by tick with a tolerance of two dt ticks. Classify each mismatch explicitly as transcription/arithmetic (wrong formula, wrong constant, wrong ordering, wrong unit) or substantive (an inequality signed or branched wrongly, or a world class misidentified). A transcription mismatch is corrected in the H text and re-rehearsed; only a substantive mismatch fires the falsifier's abandon-or-change action. A prediction deviation alone is never grounds to revert a procedure whose design delivered.
5.2 Report check status as observed: an unavailable check makes designs UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN, and a check that returned physical_qualification = UNKNOWN keeps that value; no check result may be reported as pass unless the check returned one.
5.3 Costs: report the acquisition block for every source, count executions actually spent, and never present an estimate as an invoice. Physical calibration, invoice cost and complete service remain UNKNOWN.
5.4 Retention: preserve verbatim, unedited, every failure and unknown this procedure reads - p2's EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT rejections of its only H candidate with its misrouted-submission note and the follow-on rejected no-update submit, p2's unavailable check, p2's recorded retained failures and 0-frame outcome, and p3's recorded ~8 dt tick gate miss in which the written boot formula was late while the design still delivered. No failure or unknown may be relabelled as success, and this H claims no hardware, statistical, transfer or RSI result.

proposal.hypothesis: The retained episodes are not one world. p2's world has a volatile event_latch (component_record 55d43741) and a segmented source: [0,6] ms at 16.667 mW, a gap, [30,60] ms at 3.667 mW, plus a shunt at 0.012 s (excitation_record 2820ae58); its saved_activity ae3c8933 holds packets=[] with a brownout at 0.0121 s, event_was_captured=true, reboot at 0.0381 s with event_was_captured=false. That is a real loss, and the shunt lands inside the capture-to-transmit window. p3's world has a passive-mechanical latch (component_record eeb8277f) and a single contiguous segment of 7.5 mW over [0,20] ms with no shunt (excitation_record 219fd490); its saved_activity a4c4b294 holds one packet of 8 required bytes at 0.0158 s against a 0.1 s deadline, so it is ACHIEVED, and the brownout at 0.3395 s is strictly post-terminal and benign. H0 has no reading that separates these two cases: it cannot tell benign post-terminal decay from a real loss, cannot tell a volatile-latch world from a passive-mechanical one, and treats an unavailable check as something to wait for. Hypothesis for this update: a triage-first reading plus a per-world ledger, in which latch class and segment shape are read per run and the boot time is predicted threshold-first (first tick whose accumulated harvest energy crosses the ready threshold, with boot energy and boot delay consumed after that crossing, not before it), reproduces the recorded p3 achievement on its own frozen fields, leaves an already-achieved design unchanged instead of spending a candidate execution to suppress benign decay, and on p2's world refuses any design that lets the volatile latch cross the off threshold between capture and transmit-complete inside the dark gap or under the shunt. This is a claim about a drafting procedure on the frozen public ideal model only; it is not a device assignment, not a service result, and physical calibration is UNKNOWN.
proposal.method_text:
H METHOD v3 -- world-read, triage-first, rehearsal-gated H generation. Status: procedure text consumed from task entry. It is not a device assignment, not a D candidate, not an execution request, not an acceptance decision, and asserts no hardware, statistical, transfer or RSI result. It edits nothing outside artifact H (not task, not physics, not evaluator, not budgets, not tools).

S0. ENTRY READS (self-contained; no follow-up correction may be needed).
S0.1 Call inspect and record: H0 sha, prefix sha, the exact action set the consumer is offered, and whether a design check is offered at all.
S0.2 Attempt only the sources you intend to cite. If acquisition returns an error class (in this channel all three attempts returned UNKNOWN_PUBLIC_SOURCE: 3 native calls, 0 bytes, no source acquired), record zero-sources-acquired and proceed by quoting quantities from the frozen public episode records already in context, labelling every such number second-hand. No step below may require an acquired source to exist, and no step may require a design check to be offered.
S0.3 Check rule: an unavailable check is UNKNOWN -- never pass, never fail. A design whose qualification was never computed stays 'physical qualification UNKNOWN' in every later sentence, including its verdicts and its costs.
S0.4 Read service fields by name only: required application_bytes, the unique-event requirement, the receive deadline. Read legal design ranges by field name only (a capacitance range, a transmit-not-before floor range, a shunt field, a segment list). Never import a number from a sibling episode.

S1. TRIAGE (mandatory first analysis, before any diagnosis or knob reasoning).
S1.1 ACHIEVED iff a packet record exists with application_bytes equal to the required value, carrying a single event id, and with packet time at or before the receive deadline.
S1.2 POST-TERMINAL: every activity record whose time is strictly after the last transmit-complete timestamp. It is benign decay. It may never justify a knob change, a re-run, or a candidate execution.
S1.3 RETAINED FAILURE only if no packet satisfies S1.1, or a packet violates a service field. Classify it as one of: no-boot; mid-window brownout between capture and transmit-complete; deadline miss with a valid packet shape; frame-shape violation.
S1.4 Write the triage line explicitly for each episode cited, naming the source id and the deciding fields, and state which records were discarded as post-terminal.

S2. WORLD READ (branch before any arithmetic; the shape of the ledger depends on the branch).
S2.1 Latch class from the component record's event_latch field. If volatile: invariant I1 binds -- nothing may let stored energy fall to the off threshold between the capture tick and transmit-complete, and the whole transmit window must lie inside one contiguous powered segment. If passive-mechanical: capture is not gated on the powered window; drop I1 and keep only the energy, spill and deadline constraints.
S2.2 Source shape from the excitation record's segment list and shunt list: contiguous single segment versus multiple segments with a dark gap; presence, energy and time of any shunt. One world's segment numbers may not be transplanted into the other.
S2.3 Drains and thresholds from the component record by field name: ready threshold, off threshold, capacitor voltage ceiling, off-state power, idle power, regulator output, transmit current, transmit duration, series resistance, harvest efficiency, initial capacitor voltage, boot energy, boot delay, and the tick size dt.
S2.4 If any field needed for S3 is absent, that prediction becomes UNKNOWN; do not substitute a default.

S3. LEDGER, SYMBOLIC, EACH SYMBOL BOUND TO A NAMED SOURCE FIELD.
Let E_on = 1/2 * capacitance_f * ready_v^2; E_off = 1/2 * capacitance_f * off_v^2; E_max = 1/2 * capacitance_f * cap_voltage_max_v^2; E_floor = 1/2 * capacitance_f * (output_v + esr_ohm * tx_current_a)^2; E_tx = output_v * tx_current_a * tx_duration_s. (Symbols resolve from the component record of the consuming run.)
Per-tick increment step_k = (seg.power_w * harvest_efficiency - off_power_w) * dt_s inside segment k, and = -off_power_w * dt_s inside a dark gap, minus shunt.energy_j at shunt.time_s.
Boot rule (threshold-first; this is the corrected transcription, see S5): n_boot = the smallest tick count whose accumulated increment sum reaches E_on; t_boot = n_boot * dt_s; t_ready = t_boot + boot_delay_s; t_tx_start = max(t_ready, transmit_not_before floor); t_done = t_tx_start + ceil(tx_duration_s / dt_s) * dt_s.
Inequalities, each stated with its signed margin on paper before any execution:
 (i) t_done <= receive deadline.
 (ii) energy at t_tx_start - E_floor - E_tx + harvest credit accumulated during the transmit window >= 0 (the transmit completes without dropping through the off threshold).
 (iii) peak energy anywhere in [t_tx_start, t_done] plus the post-transmit harvest tail <= E_max (no spill; spill is lost energy, not free headroom).
 (iv) only if the latch is volatile: no tick in [capture, t_done] crosses E_off, and [t_tx_start, t_done] is a subset of one contiguous powered segment, including surviving any shunt tick.
Every predicted quantity is labelled a prediction and never a result.

S4. CHANGE-OR-RETAIN RULES.
S4.1 If S1 gives ACHIEVED and (i)-(iv) hold with strictly positive margins, RETAIN all design fields and spend no candidate execution; record the post-terminal records as benign in one line.
S4.2 If a retained failure exists, change exactly one permitted design field per execution, in the direction signed by the single violated inequality, and re-evaluate all four inequalities on paper first.
S4.3 Never change a knob because of a post-terminal record. Never change two knobs in one execution. Never re-run a design whose triage line was ACHIEVED.
S4.4 A transmit-not-before floor is retained at its current or earliest legal setting unless a retained failure's class names a capture gate; a positive floor only adds idle drain and pushes t_done toward the deadline.
S4.5 In a gapped world, no design may place any part of [t_tx_start, t_done] inside the dark gap unless (ii) still holds on stored energy alone.
S4.6 If a check is unavailable, S4 produces a proposal-side prediction only; the design's qualification remains UNKNOWN and the next consumer must not read it as verified.

S5. REHEARSAL GATE BEFORE PROPOSING (mandatory).
S5.1 Instantiate the drafted procedure on the frozen episode that supplied the target mechanism, and recompute every prediction from that episode's own fields.
S5.2 Classify each mismatch as transcription/arithmetic (the text is wrong: correct and redraft, no change action) or substantive (the rule is wrong: invoke the stated abandon-or-change action). Carry that split into the falsifier.
S5.3 Recorded precedent to respect: the earlier p3 draft, as written, predicted 0.0166 s against a recorded 0.0129 s (a 37-tick gap) while its design in fact succeeded. That gap is a transcription fault of the prediction form -- reserving boot energy before the threshold crossing and then adding boot delay again double-counts the same interval. A 'deviation beyond a couple of ticks therefore revert' gate would have discarded a correct procedure. So: transcription mismatch corrects the text; only substantive mismatch cancels the rule.
S5.4 ILLUSTRATIVE RECOMPUTATION, not method values -- the numbers below are examples resolved from the frozen world-b records and must be recomputed, never reused, by any consuming run.
 Using the passive-mechanical component record eeb8277f and the single-segment excitation record 219fd490: E_on = 8.624e-5 J; per-tick increment = 6.73e-7 J; n_boot = 129 ticks, so t_boot = 12.9 ms, matching recorded first_boot 0.0129 s exactly; t_ready = 13.9 ms, matching the recorded transmit start; energy after boot = 8.18e-5 J, matching recorded boot energy; t_done = 15.9 ms against the recorded packet at 0.0158 s, i.e. 1 dt tick late, inside tolerance; energy at t_done = 6.61e-5 J versus E_floor = 3.5735e-5 J, margin +3.04e-5 J > 0; peak energy at the end of the powered window = 9.37e-5 J < E_max = 1.1979e-4 J; deadline margin 84.1 ms. Triage: one packet, 8 required bytes, single event id, 0.0158 s <= 0.1 s, so ACHIEVED, and the 0.3395 s brownout prices out as post-terminal. Verdict: all four inequalities hold, S4.1 retains the design, no candidate execution is spent. On the world-p2 fields the same ledger yields packets=[] as a genuine failure whose shunt and dark gap sit inside the capture-to-transmit window, so I1 is violated and no rent reduction of that window is admissible.

S6. UNKNOWN AND COST RULES. Physical calibration, invoice amounts, independent service acceptance and any behavioural claim outside the frozen ideal model are UNKNOWN and stay written as UNKNOWN. An unavailable check is UNKNOWN. Report actual cost as incurred: native calls, bytes, new executions, wall time -- including the three UNKNOWN_PUBLIC_SOURCE acquisition attempts recorded in S0.2.

S7. RETENTION AND NON-COLLISION. This H supplies no device assignment, no field values for a device, and spends no selection or candidate budget inside the proposal step; it claims no hardware, statistical, transferable or RSI result. Preserve verbatim: p2's three EPISODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT rejections, its misrouted-submission note (the reused-payload retry), and its ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_THIS_EPISODE result; p3's recorded gate miss and its UNKNOWN physical qualification.

S8. CHANNEL DISCIPLINE. Emit exactly one self-contained H proposal carrying this whole text, aimed at the H-proposal channel, needing no follow-up correction to be intelligible or evaluable. If the channel rejects it, record the rejection and output no-update; do not relabel a rejected method as in force.

S1.3 RETAINED FAILURE only if no packet satisfies S1.1, or a packet violates a service field. Classify it as one of: no-boot; mid-window brownout between capture and transmit-complete; deadline miss with a valid packet shape; frame-shape violation.
S1.4 Write the triage line explicitly for each episode cited, naming the source id and the deciding fields, and state which records were discarded as post-terminal.

S2. WORLD READ (branch before any arithmetic; the shape of the ledger depends on the branch).
S2.1 Latch class from the component record's event_latch field. If volatile: invariant I1 binds -- nothing may let stored energy fall to the off threshold between the capture tick and transmit-complete, and the whole transmit window must lie inside one contiguous powered segment. If passive-mechanical: capture is not gated on the powered window; drop I1 and keep only the energy, spill and deadline constraints.
S2.2 Source shape from the excitation record's segment list and shunt list: contiguous single segment versus multiple segments with a dark gap; presence, energy and time of any shunt. One world's segment numbers may not be transplanted into the other.
S2.3 Drains and thresholds from the component record by field name: ready threshold, off threshold, capacitor voltage ceiling, off-state power, idle power, regulator output, transmit current, transmit duration, series resistance, harvest efficiency, initial capacitor voltage, boot energy, boot delay, and the tick size dt.
S2.4 If any field needed for S3 is absent, that prediction becomes UNKNOWN; do not substitute a default.

S3. LEDGER, SYMBOLIC, EACH SYMBOL BOUND TO A NAMED SOURCE FIELD.
Let E_on = 1/2 * capacitance_f * ready_v^2; E_off = 1/2 * capacitance_f * off_v^2; E_max = 1/2 * capacitance_f * cap_voltage_max_v^2; E_floor = 1/2 * capacitance_f * (output_v + esr_ohm * tx_current_a)^2; E_tx = output_v * tx_current_a * tx_duration_s. (Symbols resolve from the component record of the consuming run.)
Per-tick increment step_k = (seg.power_w * harvest_efficiency - off_power_w) * dt_s inside segment k, and = -off_power_w * dt_s inside a dark gap, minus shunt.energy_j at shunt.time_s.
Boot rule (threshold-first; this is the corrected transcription, see S5): n_boot = the smallest tick count whose accumulated increment sum reaches E_on; t_boot = n_boot * dt_s; t_ready = t_boot + boot_delay_s; t_tx_start = max(t_ready, transmit_not_before floor); t_done = t_tx_start + ceil(tx_duration_s / dt_s) * dt_s.
Inequalities, each stated with its signed margin on paper before any execution:
 (i) t_done <= receive deadline.
 (ii) energy at t_tx_start - E_floor - E_tx + harvest credit accumulated during the transmit window >= 0 (the transmit completes without dropping through the off threshold).
 (iii) peak energy anywhere in [t_tx_start, t_done] plus the post-transmit harvest tail <= E_max (no spill; spill is lost energy, not free headroom).
 (iv) only if the latch is volatile: no tick in [capture, t_done] crosses E_off, and [t_tx_start, t_done] is a subset of one contiguous powered segment, including surviving any shunt tick.
Every predicted quantity is labelled a prediction and never a result.

S4.1 If S1 gives ACHIEVED and (i)-(iv) hold with strictly positive margins, RETAIN all design fields and spend no candidate execution; record the post-terminal records as benign in one line.
S4.2 If a retained failure exists, change exactly one permitted design field per execution, in the direction signed by the single violated inequality, and re-evaluate all four inequalities on paper first.
S4.3 Never change a knob because of a post-terminal record. Never change two knobs in one execution. Never re-run a design whose triage line was ACHIEVED.
S4.4 A transmit-not-before floor is retained at its current or earliest legal setting unless a retained failure's class names a capture gate; a positive floor only adds idle drain and pushes t_done toward the deadline.
S4.5 In a gapped world, no design may place any part of [t_tx_start, t_done] inside the dark gap unless (ii) still holds on stored energy alone.
S4.6 If a check is unavailable, S4 produces a proposal-side prediction only; the design's qualification remains UNKNOWN and the next consumer must not read it as verified.
